prompt: A Java service has stopped responding. Its CPU use is near 0%. What's the most useful first step?

options.text: Restart it immediately and look at the logs afterwards
options.explanation: Restarting loses the live state, so collect evidence first when operationally feasible. Existing dumps, core files and detailed logs may preserve useful evidence after restart.

options.text: Take two or three thread dumps a few seconds apart and compare them
options.explanation: Correct. Threads stuck at the same lock call in every dump are genuinely blocked, and `jstack` will also print any Java-level deadlock it finds.

options.text: Attach a CPU profiler to find the hot loop
options.explanation: With near-zero CPU there's no hot loop to find. A profiler suits livelock or busy loops, where CPU is high.

options.text: Increase the thread pool size so new requests can be served
options.explanation: If the threads are deadlocked, new threads will soon hit the same locks and join the cycle's waiters. It hides the symptom for minutes, not the cause.

workedExample: Near-zero CPU suggests waiting, which may be deadlock, a lost wake-up or a slow dependency. Capture several thread dumps and inspect current wait/ownership relations. Repeated stacks alone do not prove deadlock; changing stacks do not prove useful progress. Java can identify supported platform-thread monitor/synchronizer cycles. Preserve evidence before restarting when feasible.
